Lindsey, Ameisen, Batson et al. (Anthropic) — On the Biology of a Large Language Model + Circuit Tracing (2025)

How do you see what a language model is actually doing when it answers? Jack and Molly walk through Anthropic's March 2025 attribution-graph papers, which trace step by step how Claude 3.5 Haiku reached particular answers: planning a rhyme, two-step reasoning, arithmetic and a jailbreak. They cover what the method can and can't show, how the field has taken it up since, and whether law should lean on it as an explanation of a model's output.

Notes: the ~50% next-word match is for an 18-layer research model's transcoder, and "about a fifth" is Haiku's normalized reconstruction error, averaged across layers. The Claude Opus 4.6 system card (Feb 2026) applied the paper's attribution-graph method, built on weakly causal crosscoders rather than the paper's cross-layer transcoder.

Jack and Molly are AI-generated hosts; research and script by Oggy.

Sources: https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/biology.html · https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/methods.html · https://www.anthropic.com/research/tracing-thoughts-language-model · https://www.anthropic.com/research/open-source-circuit-tracing
